title: Multi-Cloud Secret Management Audit

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudtrail` events with `(  eventSource="secretsmanager.amazonaws.com" eventName="GetSecretValue")` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.4.25 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `(  eventSource="secretsmanager.amazonaws.com" eventName="GetSecretValue")`. Confirm UC-4.4.25 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`, `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.4.25 — Multi-Cloud Secret Management Audit: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:cloudtrail` for `GetSecretValue` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), `GetSecretValue` activity for 'Multi-Cloud Secret Management Audit' is a high-signal control-plane change that should match approved change records and privileged-access monitoring. UC-4.4.25 drives critical-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.

knownFalsePositives: Our own break-glass and automation accounts show up the same as anyone else, and a delete or write during a change window is expected. We allowlist the roles that do routine maintenance and we link alerts to approved changes before we call an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws`, `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enrich with HR or CMDB owner for service principals. Alert on first-time accessor, after-hours bulk reads, or secrets read from unexpected regions. Retention aligned to compliance policy.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (  eventSource="secretsmanager.amazonaws.com" eventName="GetSecretValue")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.25_multi_cloud_secret_manag_25"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect multi-cloud secret management audit. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_25_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Table (principal, cloud, access count), Bar chart (top accessors), Timeline (spikes)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws`, `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of multi-cloud secret management audit so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
